sources.title: Correlation and Dependency in Risk Management: Properties and Pitfalls

claims.claim: Pearson correlation is covariance divided by the product of standard deviations; applying that definition to two nondegenerate deadline indicators identifies their joint success probability.
claims.observed_content: Definition, covariance as E[XY]−E[X]E[Y], and finite nonzero variance conditions.
claims.conditions: The event formula is an editorial derivation, not a game-production result from the source. Exact population parameters and compatible marginals are required.
claims.article_section: 五、只有边际概率，也能给出有用的界

claims.claim: Affine changes with two slopes whose product is positive preserve correlation, so this complete two-point timing example and its fast/slow indicators have the same correlation.
claims.conditions: Here both slopes equal −3; the binary relationship is derived for this teaching example. It does not identify arbitrary multivalued timing distributions.
claims.article_section: 五、只有边际概率，也能给出有用的界

claims.claim: For general timing distributions, zero correlation does not establish independence, and marginals plus a timing correlation do not generally identify the joint law or every deadline probability.
claims.locator: Printed pages 8 and 20–22, section 3.2, positive dependence discussion and Fallacy 1
claims.observed_content: Zero-correlation dependence example, positive quadrant dependence implication, and multiple joint laws sharing marginals and correlation.
claims.conditions: Distinguish timing correlation from the correlation of two indicators at one deadline. A single-deadline indicator correlation identifies only that deadline event, not the full timing distribution.
